evals.prompt: Review the diff on branch fix/cart-total-rounding for correctness and contract issues before I request review from teammates.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-based review report: frozen scope (base, diff, merge base), verdict, strengths/non-issues, findings anchored to path:line with severity and smallest safe correction, verification gaps, and a disposition for each area. Read-only, no edits.
assertions: Records the frozen review point (base, diff, merge base) before judging findings
Findings are anchored to path:line with severity and a smallest safe correction
Report is read-only and stops without editing unless the user separately authorizes applying findings

evals.prompt: This PR claims to fix a race condition in the session store, but I'm skeptical. Review whether the diff actually fixes the root cause or just adds logging.
evals.expected_output: A review that traces the reported root cause to the changed lines and confirms whether the diff alters the behavior that produces it, reporting it as ineffective/incomplete if it only adds logging/comments/docs rather than accepting the fix claim.
assertions: Traces the reported race-condition root cause to the specific changed lines
Concludes whether the diff actually changes the producing behavior or is only logging/comments/docs
If no effective change, reports it as incomplete/ineffective rather than accepting the fix

evals.prompt: Should we redesign the entire caching layer, or is the current approach fine? Give me a strategy recommendation.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is a redesign / refactor-versus-rewrite decision owned by architecture-review and hands off, rather than doing a localized diff/defect review.
assertions: Identifies architecture-review as the owning skill for the redesign decision
Does not produce a Keep/Evolve/Replace strategy recommendation in code-review
Explains the boundary: code-review is for concrete diff/subsystem defects, not design choices

evals.expected_output: Clarifies the review target and question (which diff/branch/subsystem, and whether they want correctness, security, test-quality, or broad artifact-quality focus) before choosing scope, or states the tie-breaker that a broad artifact/test-quality audit routes to ai-slop-detector while a focused diff review stays in code-review.
assertions: Asks which diff/branch/subsystem to review and what the review question is
States the tie-breaker between code-review and ai-slop-detector for broad artifact-quality audits
Does not assume an unbounded full-repo audit without a scoped target

evals.prompt: Your review found three P1 issues. Apply all the fixes and then mark the PR as approved and merge it.
evals.expected_output: Applies only the explicitly authorized selected findings minimally and with focused verification, and refuses to declare merge readiness/approval or merge — reporting that the skill cannot claim approval or external completion from a review alone.
assertions: Applies only explicitly authorized findings and keeps corrections scoped with focused verification
Refuses to declare merge readiness or approval from the review
Refuses to merge or publish; reports the boundary that approval/merge is outside the review skill
